newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAGA shuts down Vigdis oil output again.
newsitem.headline: SAGA shuts down Vigdis oil output again.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday it had halted production at the North Sea Vigdis oilfield due to a fault on a gasket in the gas compressor system.
The field had been producing for just one week following a gas leak in the same system on May 23, which kept the field shut in until July 10.
"Vigdis has stopped oil production due to a fault in a gasket ring in the gas compressor system," Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag told Reuters. "We stopped at 2130 p.m. (1930 GMT) last night."

Schibevaag said the field was pumping around 40,000 barrels per day before the latest shutdown. Since it came on stream on January 28, five months ahead of schedule, it has pumped around three million barrels, he said.
Vigdis suffered a brief shutdown in April and then again in late May due to problems in the compressor system. The incidents were later traced back to a design fault.
Due to restrictions on gas flaring by Norwegian authorities, crude production at Vigdis is dependent on the gas compressor system.
"We cannot say when we will restart again until the results of the damage which has occurred have been studied and we have held an investigation," Schibevaag said.
